classification_rules.gate_normalization: parsed := btrim(lower(structured_data->>'registration_number')); row := btrim(lower(e.row_skrasnr)); VERIFIED needs equality (exact mirror of migration.sql verified_company_observation and the PDF_COMPANY_MISMATCH* review branches)
classification_rules.digits_only_secondary: digits-only equality recorded when it differs from the gate; never upgrades a state; NO fuzzy fallback (name/address/person/date are not attribution)
classification_rules.VERIFIED: parse exists AND parsed regnr non-blank AND normalize(parsed)==normalize(row_skrasnr)
classification_rules.MISSING_PARSED_REGNR: parse exists but parsed regnr null/blank
classification_rules.NO_PARSE_RESULT: document has observation(s) but no parse_result for parser_version '1'
classification_rules.NO_OBSERVATION: document related to source row but has no observation
classification_rules.AMBIGUOUS_MULTIPLE_PARSE_RESULTS: same observation has >1 parse_result for the same parser_version (no latest-wins invented)
classification_rules.multiple_parser_versions: reported separately per relation; relation state uses validation parser_version '1'

population.relation_vs_document_note: relations are N:M: a document reachable from several source rows is counted once in documents but once per relation
population.event_accounting_note: every source event in the corpus has at least one relation, so relation-state classification covers 100% of events; nothing outside the relation population can reach derived history unclssified

observation_multiplicity.note: documents re-observed in later runs have one observation (and its own parse result) per run; each relation is classified across ALL its observations with fail-closed precedence; no latest-wins

requested_vs_row.note: requested_regnr vs row_skrasnr; the attribution gate uses row_skrasnr only

snapshot_leak.snapshot_view_kind: VIEW (recomputed live; gate can not be bypassed by stale rows)
